title: Strategic Signals Gateway and Initiative Lifeboat
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: company-level objectives are tracked across multiple dashboards (Console metrics, OKR sheets, delivery trackers). Signals that an initiative is drifting (velocity drop, unexpected bug volume, missed milestones) are noisy and siloed, so escalation and reallocation decisions are slow.

Proposal: build a lightweight 'Strategic Signals Gateway' (SSG) and a paired 'Initiative Lifeboat' playbook. SSG ingests normalized signals from telemetry (Console SLO/latency dashboards), delivery trackers (Linear/Velocity), and qualitative inputs (PM/Design flags). It evaluates rules and surface-level heuristics and emits a compact risk signal per company initiative (green/amber/red) with a short rationale. The Initiative Lifeboat is an operational protocol and small budget/time reserve for rapid triage: temporary resource shifts, canary rollbacks, or scope reductions to preserve key OKR outcomes.

Scope: MVP focused on company-level OKRs (top 8 objectives) and their top-level initiatives (approx 30 initiatives). MVP does not include automated remediation — only signal, notify, and human triage runbook. Integration points: Redwood Console metrics API, Linear API, and a lightweight Confluence page for audit/logs.

Why this is different: instead of a large governance process, SSG standardizes signal inputs and a short decision lane (Lifeboat) so leadership can make quick, consistent trade-offs without disrupting teams with ad-hoc escalations.

Out-of-scope for MVP: per-team micro-SLAs, automated autoscaling changes, or billing-level cost rebalancing. Those can be follow-ups once SSG proves signal fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: SSG receives and normalizes at least 4 signal types (latency SLO, error rate, Linear progress, PM flag) for all 30 initiatives
Risk state (green/amber/red) is computed and stored for each initiative on a daily cadence
A single pager 'Initiative Lifeboat' runbook exists in Confluence with triage steps, roles, and a 48-hour response SLA
Escalation notifications are sent to a preconfigured Slack channel and to initiative EPs for amber/red states
Basic audit trail is accessible (who flagged, what signals, timestamp) for every risk transition
Leadership sign-off: GTM + Eng + Product agree on risk heuristics and Lifeboat budget allocation
success_metrics: Mean time from red signal to Lifeboat action < 48 hours
Reduction in cross-org emergency meetings for top-8 OKRs by 40% in first quarter after launch
>80% of red/amber signals have an assigned owner and action within 24 hours
Signal precision: >= 70% of red signals correspond to measurable delivery or quality regressions (validated by postmortem)
stakeholders: Engineering leadership (Director of Serving Runtime, Eng Ops)
milestones: 2026-03-15: finalize signal taxonomy and risk heuristics
2026-03-22: prototype SSG data ingestion (Console + Linear) and risk engine
2026-04-05: Lifeboat runbook published + stakeholder tabletop exercise
2026-04-15: Beta signals pushed to leadership Slack channel (non-urgent mode)
risks: False positives: noisy signals might trigger unnecessary Lifeboat actions and erode trust
Signal gaps: some initiatives lack instrumentation to produce reliable metrics
Resource contention: teams may resist temporary resource reallocation without clear guardrails
Alert fatigue: too-frequent amber notifications will reduce attention from leadership
Data latency: some dashboards update slowly which could delay accurate risk state
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): instrument top-8 OKRs and ~30 initiatives; daily risk computation; notify leadership Slack channel; tabletop exercise with decision owners. Phase 2 (post-MVP): expand to 60+ initiatives, add Confluence audit pages per incident, and prototype role-based automated suggestions (not automatic remediation). Phase 3: evaluate automated short-term resource allocation flows and budgeted Lifeboat credit integration with Finance.
